item.title: Sweden summons Iranian envoy after death sentence reports
item.description: Sweden summoned the Iranian ambassador this week following reports that a Swedish citizen had been sentenced to death in Iran, the Scandinavian country's foreign minister said on Friday.

item.title: How to make a julbord if you live outside Sweden
item.description: Planning a Swedish Christmas meal – the scrumptious julbord – outside of Sweden this year? Here are The Local's tips on how you can make your own julbord, and where to source essential ingredients.

item.title: UPDATED: Courts in Sweden criticise proposal to revoke permanent residency permits
item.description: Five of Sweden's highest legal authorities have advised the government to drop a proposal to revoke permanent residency permits, warning that it risks massive costs, would overwhelm the legal system, and threatens important legal principles.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: julhög
item.description: Today's word of the day is julhög, which is made up of the word jul (Christmas) and hög (heap, pile, or mound).

item.title: Six ways to tell if you should spend Christmas in Sweden
item.description: Do you want Christmas to last as long as possible? Are you an introvert who likes predictability or an spontaneous extrovert? Here are our six criteria to check whether Sweden is the best country for you to celebrate in.

item.title: Why Sweden's Moderates are sending mixed messages on work permit immigration
item.description: In this week's podcast: how to celebrate Christmas in Sweden, Moderates split on immigration, predictions for Sweden's economy in 2026, and why has a court blocked Sweden's planned wolf hunt?

item.title: Inside Sweden: Glögg, migration politics and what to expect next
item.description: The Local's Nordic Editor Richard Orange rounds up the biggest stories of the week and wishes you all a Happy Christmas in our Inside Sweden newsletter.

item.title: What you need to know about travelling in Sweden over Christmas 2025
item.description: Christmas is one of the busiest times for travel in Sweden, whether you're travelling by air, road or rail. Here's the latest on how to travel safely and where you might face delayed trains or ugly traffic jams.

item.title: Why do Swedes play bingo the day before Christmas Eve?
item.description: Throughout history, Swedes have stayed up late the day before Christmas Eve to get everything ready for the big day of celebrations. Since 1995, this has also included playing bingo until midnight – but why?

item.title: Head of Nobel-awarding Swedish Academy resigns
item.description: The Swedish Academy said Saturday its permanent secretary, Mats Malm, is stepping down after seven years of heading the prestigious institution that awards the annual Nobel literature prize.
